items.title: a BARE closure under `print` still goes to `console.log` on JS and is refused natively (F25's function half), while a closure INSIDE an aggregate prints its written type on both backends since S3 — `print(\|x: i32\| x + 1)` should print `<closure \|i32\| i32>` on both
items.discussion: debug-49 (Order 49: S3 `print` of non-scalars; its owner question 3, rec: a follow-up that prints the closure's type on both and retires F25's function half); F25; E257 (the debugging arc)
items.body: S3 routes aggregates through the dbg printer, which already spells a closure field as `<closure |i32| i32>`; a closure as the WHOLE argument is the one shape left on the host path. Door: the analyzer records the argument's closure type for `print` as it does for dbg's per-type printers, and both emitters print the spelling; natively the refusal by name retires. Pins: both backends byte-identical; the host/opaque values keep console.log. Sizing S; debug lane.
